title: Editing the `reply_to` and `from` addresses on an email
body:
Hi there,

Is there a simple way to set custom `reply_to` email addresses with a DeviseMailer?

I'm working on a project where I need to set a differenct `reply_to` address for an email message to the `from` address, and I didn't see a particularly nice way to do this.

I'd normally expect to add it here, in a custom subclass Invite Mailer, like so:

```
class InviteMailer < Devise::Mailer

  default from: Rails.configuration.invite_from_address
  default reply: Rails.configuration.invite_reply_to_address

  def custom_invitation_instructions(record)
    devise_mail(record, :custom_invitation_instructions)
  end

end
```

But devise doesn't seem to look for reply_to addresses in `mailer_sender` method.

Also when I look into the `devise_mail` [method in devise itself](https://github.com/plataformatec/devise/blob/master/lib/devise/mailers/helpers.rb#L28), I see every property being set other than `reply_to`.

Right now, I'm getting around this by redeclaring the headers_for method like so in my custom mailer:

```
# Devise by default doesn't allow you to set the reply_to
# headers - so redeclaring this function here allows us to
# call the superclass, then override the reply_to address ourselves
def headers_for(action)
 output = super(action)
 output.merge!(:reply_to => Rails.configuration.invite_email_reply_to])
 output
end
```

But I can't be the only person needing to have different `reply_to` and `from` addresses when using devise, and I'd like to have devise pick this up like so in the mailer_sender section:

```
  def mailer_sender(mapping)
    if default_params[:from].present?
      default_params[:from]
    if default_params[:reply_to].present?
      default_params[:reply_to]          
    elsif Devise.mailer_sender.is_a?(Proc)
      Devise.mailer_sender.call(mapping.name)
    else
      Devise.mailer_sender
    end
```

But I don't quite understand what's going on in line 36. It seems like it might cover some of this already, but I'm not sure what it's for:

```
    if resource.respond_to?(:headers_for)
      headers.merge!(resource.headers_for(action))
    end
```

What is the intended use for this snippet?

Thanks

C
